author: WP13
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on the glTF vertex-byte ABI: the stride table, the vtable-inflation bug behind typed/raw upload, index narrowing, the seven topologies, tangents, mirroring and hard limits. The layouts themselves are current, but selection changed (material-model rule, coloured PBR at 60/80), the table is now canonical data queried by upload and morphing, unknown strides are refused, the index alignment hazard is fixed and missing normals are computed. None of this was on the site; it now lives on the vertex packing deep dive.

concepts.section: GPU Packing and the Stride ABI
concepts.text: ExtractMesh packs tightly into one of a fixed set of layouts and records only the stride; the upload path, renderers, morph blender and oracles must all agree on the offsets, so the stride is a de-facto ABI.

concepts.section: GPU Packing and the Stride ABI
concepts.text: At TARGET the meaning of each stride is stated once as data in VertexDeclarationFidelity.hpp's canonical table (InferredLayoutForStride).
concepts.note: The claim said the ABI is not declared anywhere as a type; TARGET has a canonical data table.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 20 is position at 0 and UV at 12, used by DualTextureEffect (reached only by an unlit base-colour-plus-occlusion primitive).
concepts.note: Which primitives reach this stride changed at TARGET (material-model rule, GLTF-462/463).

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 24 is position 0, colour u8x4 at 12, UV at 16, BasicEffect with vertex colour (unlit coloured primitives).
concepts.note: Which primitives reach this stride changed at TARGET (material-model rule, GLTF-462/463).

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 32 is position 0, normal 12, UV 24 for BasicEffect (unlit uncoloured primitives).
concepts.note: Which primitives reach this stride changed at TARGET (material-model rule, GLTF-462/463).

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 48 is position 0, normal 12, tangent vec4 at 24, UV 40 for PbrEffect.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 52 is position 0, normal 12, UV 24, weights 32, joint u8x4 at 48 for SkinnedEffect.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 56 is stride 52 plus colour at 52 for SkinnedEffect with vertex colour.
concepts.note: Which primitives reach this stride changed at TARGET (material-model rule, GLTF-462/463).

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 60 is stride 48 plus UV1 at 48 and colour at 56 for PbrEffect with two UV sets and/or COLOR_0.
concepts.note: Which primitives reach this stride changed at TARGET (material-model rule, GLTF-462/463).

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 68 is position 0, normal 12, tangent 24, UV 40, weights 48, joints 64 for SkinnedPbrEffect.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 76 is stride 68 plus UV1 at 68 for SkinnedPbrEffect with two UV sets.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 80 is stride 76 plus colour at 76 for SkinnedPbrEffect with COLOR_0.
concepts.note: Which primitives reach this stride changed at TARGET (material-model rule, GLTF-462/463).

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 60 was first a padded rigid PBR+UV1 record (56 already meant skinned+colour, one meaning per stride); its four spare bytes now carry COLOR_0, written as opaque white when absent.
tokens: one stride must have one meaning

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Stride 76 has no spare bytes, so the skinned coloured PBR record needed stride 80 with the whole stride-76 record as prefix.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Layout selection is semantic and data-driven: VertexLayoutTableEXT rows matched first-wins by skinned, coloured, PBR, dual-texture and second-UV flags; skinned rows come first.
concepts.note: The claim described the rule as an expression; TARGET encodes it as an enumerable table.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: The PBR flag is the material model: every material except KHR_materials_unlit selects a PBR layout, so coloured metallic-roughness primitives take 60/80 and strides 24/56 are reached only by unlit materials.
concepts.note: The claim said colour selects 24 unless skinning selects 56; at TARGET a coloured metallic-roughness primitive keeps PBR.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: PBR layouts widen to carry a second independently selected UV set and COLOR_0.
tokens: widened to 76 for two sampled UV sets

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Missing UVs default to (0,0) and missing colour alpha to 255; missing normals are computed rather than defaulted.
tokens: missing normals are computed rather than defaulted
concepts.note: Normals are no longer a stable default at TARGET.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: Each table row names what it cannot carry (stride 24: normals; stride 20: normals and tangents), and that downgrade is reported.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: The table's tests walk every flag combination, check each stride carries what is asked, that lossy rows explain themselves, and that the corpus agrees with the table.

concepts.section: The ten glTF layouts
concepts.text: The upload switch also recognises stride 16 (typed VertexPositionColor for non-glTF content), so the canonical table has eleven entries while the glTF importer emits ten; the two counts must not be merged.
tokens: the canonical table has eleven entries and the glTF importer emits ten

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: CNA vertex structs derive from polymorphic IVertexType, so sizeof exceeds the clean layout and the first field need not be at byte 0; reinterpreting packed bytes as such structs shifts every field.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: That object-layout error was the root cause of a long-running invisible-model symptom family.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: Strides 16, 20, 24 and 32 are reconstructed field-by-field as typed vertex objects before typed SetData.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: Strides 48, 52, 56, 60, 68, 76 and 80 use VertexBuffer::SetDataRaw, preserving the packed bytes.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: Every buffer is created with a VertexDeclaration built from the canonical table entry, so renderers see the real element list.
tokens: VertexDeclaration built from the same canonical table entry

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: A stride outside the canonical table throws ContentLoadException instead of returning an unfilled vertex buffer; a hand-written .cnj naming another stride is refused.
concepts.note: Formerly an unlisted stride silently produced an empty buffer.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: Seven stride-inferring renderers (Vulkan, Software, WebGPU, SDL_GPU and the three Direct3D renderers) choose native layouts from a stride table, so the fidelity header is a safety boundary that refuses declarations the native layout cannot represent.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: The fidelity rule is asymmetric: record advance equals stride, no native fetch reads a declared element's bytes under another meaning, each declared element has a matching native attribute, elements fit and do not overlap; undeclared native attributes are allowed.
tokens: A native attribute the declaration does not name is not a violation

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: EasyGL is checked against the selected stock program's ordered input list because it binds elements by declaration index and its programs give one location different meanings per stride.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: The canonical table is queried by the upload path and the morph blender, but the importer's selection rows, renderer native layouts and the L5 golden tables still state the ABI independently.
concepts.note: The claim called the table a safety oracle only; TARGET also derives upload declarations and morph offsets from it.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: The L5 golden layout table is stated twice (generator STRIDE_LAYOUTS and C++ oracle) and a test compares them, because a table stated once cannot catch its own drift.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: CI runs the imported-stride declaration check and RendererStrideConformance on STUB, HEADLESS, OPENGLES3, VULKAN and SOFTWARE; a renderer that cannot bind a colour-carrying PBR stride must refuse by name.

concepts.section: Why ordinary C++ structs were unsafe
concepts.text: Generating every view from one declarative source remains a possible refactor; independently stated tables compared by tests are worth more than comments claiming agreement.
tokens: Generating every view from one declarative source

concepts.section: Indices: source width is not destination width
concepts.text: CNA decodes glTF indices itself because cgltf's helper returns 0 with no error channel for sparse accessors — the cause of defect D4.

concepts.section: Indices: source width is not destination width
concepts.text: The index decoder accepts unsigned byte, short and int scalars, honours view/accessor offsets and sparse overrides, reads with memcpy for unaligned views, uses overflow-safe spans and names the offending value in errors.

concepts.section: Indices: source width is not destination width
concepts.text: A non-indexed primitive receives the implicit sequence 0..n-1.

concepts.section: Indices: source width is not destination width
concepts.text: Every index is proved below the vertex count before use; only then is the GPU width chosen: 16 bits for at most 65,535 packed vertices, 32 bits above.

concepts.section: Indices: source width is not destination width
concepts.text: The source component type is irrelevant: a 100-vertex mesh with 32-bit source indices becomes a 16-bit buffer, made safe by the range proof.
tokens: source component type is deliberately irrelevant

concepts.section: Indices: source width is not destination width
concepts.text: The width decision uses the packed vertex count, which can exceed the source count when flat normals split vertices; the .cnj reader applies the same rule to its sidecars.

concepts.section: Indices: source width is not destination width
concepts.text: Casting vector<uint8_t>::data() to uint16_t*/uint32_t* before IndexBuffer::SetData was a misaligned typed access.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: ContentManager.cpp IndicesFromBytes<TIndex> memcpys the index bytes into properly typed storage (GLTF-037) and BuildModelMeshPartGeometryEXT uploads from it for the glTF, .cnj and .cnb routes; the page keeps it only as a historical sharp edge.

concepts.section: All seven topology modes have an explicit route
concepts.text: ClassifyPrimitiveTopology maps glTF modes 0-6 and throws for any other mode rather than assuming triangles.

concepts.section: All seven topology modes have an explicit route
concepts.text: Points, lines and line strips keep their topology; a line loop becomes a closed line strip; triangle strips and fans become winding-correct triangle lists (D5 fixed).

concepts.section: All seven topology modes have an explicit route
concepts.text: The part's CNAEXT PrimitiveType travels through the direct, .cnj and .cnb routes, and primitive counts follow the topology (n/3, n/2, n-1, n).

concepts.section: All seven topology modes have an explicit route
concepts.text: An incomplete final primitive or too-short run is dropped and counted; conversions are reported as topology-converted and tails as incomplete-indices-dropped.

concepts.section: All seven topology modes have an explicit route
concepts.text: Draco-compressed primitives are restricted to triangle lists and strips by the extension's own rules.

concepts.section: Tangents and winding
concepts.text: An authored TANGENT is preserved on PBR layouts; legacy _TANGENT/_BINORMAL pairs import with derived handedness; an authored tangent is ignored when normals were generated.

concepts.section: Tangents and winding
concepts.text: Otherwise ComputeTangentsEXT uses position/UV gradients from the UV set the normal map samples, skips degenerate-UV triangles, weights by corner angle and Gram-Schmidt-orthogonalises.

concepts.section: Tangents and winding
concepts.text: The tangent generator is intentionally not bit-exact MikkTSpace: it keeps one tangent per glTF vertex and does not weld corners across matching seams.

concepts.section: Tangents and winding
concepts.text: Only PBR strides have a tangent slot, so an authored tangent on another layout is dropped and reported.

concepts.section: Tangents and winding
concepts.text: Missing normals are computed as flat normals with vertex splitting; nearly parallel faces merged within tolerance are reported.

concepts.section: Tangents and winding
concepts.text: No coordinate conversion is needed, but a placement with a negative-determinant transform mirrors the mesh and reverses front faces.

concepts.section: Tangents and winding
concepts.text: CNA records the mirror fact per placement (mirrored-winding-unapplied) but does not change cull state; flipping the shared index buffer would break unmirrored placements, so default culling can hide such a placement.

concepts.section: Tangents and winding
concepts.text: Cull state is caller-owned device state, as for the carried doubleSided flag; this boundary is separate from tangent handedness.

concepts.section: Hard limits carried by the bytes
concepts.text: At most two distinct source UV sets reach PBR effects; a third is reported as uv-set-mismatch on both runtime and offline paths.
concepts.note: The runtime path now reports it too.

concepts.section: Hard limits carried by the bytes
concepts.text: Only JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0 are imported (four influences); extra sets are dropped with the worst weight reported and remaining weights renormalised.

concepts.section: Hard limits carried by the bytes
concepts.text: Joint indices are four unsigned bytes; the remapped index is checked against 255 so it cannot wrap.

concepts.section: Hard limits carried by the bytes
concepts.text: SkinnedEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect cap palettes at 72 (MaxBones); a skin with more joints is refused at import.
concepts.note: Larger skins are refused at import rather than left to fail later.

concepts.section: Hard limits carried by the bytes
concepts.text: Morph targets are CPU-blended into the base bytes and re-uploaded; position, normal and tangent offsets come from the canonical table; morphed texture coordinates and colours are dropped and reported.

concepts.section: Hard limits carried by the bytes
concepts.text: Only COLOR_0 is imported.

concepts.section: Hard limits carried by the bytes
concepts.text: These limits are different layers: raising the palette would not widen a byte index, and widening the index would not add a fifth influence or third UV set; any format change must update the whole ABI and its oracles together.
tokens: These are different layers of limit

issues.text: The misaligned uint16_t*/uint32_t* cast of index bytes before IndexBuffer::SetData is absent at TARGET (IndicesFromBytes memcpy, GLTF-037).
Mirrored (negative-determinant) placements are not winding-corrected; under default culling they can disappear. Reported per placement.
Only two distinct UV sets, four joint influences and one colour set are carried by the vertex ABI.
